issues.legal_issue: Persons inducted onto land by someone who has lost the right to possess it cannot obtain tenant protection merely by cultivating the land.
material_facts: A decree established an adopted son’s right to the land and to possession of it.
After the decree, the widow who had been dispossessed of the land leased it to the claimants, although she no longer had a right to possess or lease the land.
The claimants sought restoration of possession on the basis that they had cultivated the land as tenants.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were not entitled to tenant protection because they had been inducted by a person who was a trespasser when she inducted them, and they could not be regarded as lawfully cultivating the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 32(1), 2(v) and 5 of the Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, a claim for possession as a tenant requires the relevant tenant status, and deemed tenancy under Section 5 requires lawful cultivation. The meaning of “asami shikmi” referred to in Section 2(13) of the Hyderabad Land Revenue Act requires a lessee holding under a written instrument or oral agreement, but an agreement with someone who has no right to possess the land cannot confer the claimed protection. Dahya Lal v. Rasul Mohammed Abdul Hakim was distinguished because the tenant there had been lawfully inducted by a mortgagee in possession acting in the ordinary course of management. Mohima Chunder Saha v. Hazari Pramanik and Binad Lal Pakrashi v. Kalu Pramanik were distinguished because they applied the different protective scheme of the Bengal Tenancy Act.

rule.if: tenant_possession_restoration_claim and claim_based_on_cultivation and induction_after_loss_of_possessory_right and inducer_lacked_authority_to_lease

predicates.tenant_possession_restoration_claim: The cultivators sought restoration of possession on a claim to tenant status.
predicates.claim_based_on_cultivation: The cultivators relied on their cultivation of the land as the basis for claiming tenant protection.
predicates.induction_after_loss_of_possessory_right: The person who placed the cultivators on the land did so after a decree had established another person's right to the land and possession.
predicates.inducer_lacked_authority_to_lease: When placing the cultivators on the land, the person who inducted them had no right to possess or lease it.

issues.definition: When cultivators seek restored possession based on cultivation as tenants, and they were inducted by someone who had already lost the right to possess and lacked authority to lease the land, tenant protection is unavailable.
